mondayClosures.generalNote: Most Staatliche Museen zu Berlin (state museum) houses follow the same Monday closure as the confirmed list above.
mondayClosures.source: Verified against Deutsches Technikmuseum and Berlin Wall Memorial official visitor information on 23 July 2026; the museum closure list follows the Berlin Monday Plan Checker.

sundayRule.generalNote: Regular shops are closed all day Sunday by German law. Bakeries, some kiosks, museum shops and Sunday-open exceptions inside train stations (Hauptbahnhof, Alexanderplatz, Friedrichstraße, Zoologischer Garten) are the usual exceptions.
sundayRule.exceptionsNote: v1 does not carry a dated 'verkaufsoffener Sonntag' exception list. Berlin's citywide Sunday-shopping dates are announced by district and by half-year (2026 H2 and all of 2027 were not fully published as of the 2026-08-20 check), so a partial list would go stale and mislead rather than help. The general Sunday rule above is always safe to show.

bookingDeadlines.label: The Reichstag dome
bookingDeadlines.urgentNote: The Reichstag dome is free but registration only, and it fills first. Put it in this week.
bookingDeadlines.comfortableClause: The Reichstag dome is still comfortable at this range.
bookingDeadlines.source: bundestag.de visitor registration guidance: popular slots fill within the first week of release in summer, book 4-6 weeks out in shoulder season, 2-3 weeks out in winter; berlin-booking-deadline-planner treats it as 'the first free slot to secure'

bookingDeadlines.label: Museum Island timed slots
bookingDeadlines.urgentNote: Museum Island timed-entry tickets are close to selling out for your dates. Book the one museum you actually care about now.
bookingDeadlines.comfortableClause: Museum Island timed slots are still comfortable at this range.
bookingDeadlines.source: berlin-booking-deadline-planner: 'book when a specific museum or rainy-day block matters, otherwise keep one museum slot flexible'

bookingDeadlines.label: Sanssouci Palace
bookingDeadlines.urgentNote: Sanssouci Palace uses fixed entry times and a limited daily ticket count. Book the interior slot now if that is the reason for your day trip.
bookingDeadlines.comfortableClause: Sanssouci Palace is still comfortable at this range.
bookingDeadlines.source: berlin-booking-deadline-planner: 'Sanssouci and some palace visits use fixed entry times or limited daily tickets, buy earlier if the palace interior is the reason for the day'

bookingDeadlines.label: TV Tower
bookingDeadlines.urgentNote: The TV Tower is worth booking now only if you want a fixed time, the restaurant, or a sunset slot.
bookingDeadlines.comfortableClause: The TV Tower is still comfortable at this range.
bookingDeadlines.source: berlin-booking-deadline-planner: 'worth booking early only for a fixed time, restaurant plan, sunset slot or very short trip, otherwise flexibility can beat an early paid ticket'

bookingDeadlines.label: Concerts, shows or festivals on your dates
bookingDeadlines.urgentNote: If there is a concert, match or festival you already have in mind for your dates, that hard ticket is the easiest thing to lose by waiting. Secure it before you plan the rest of the day around it.
bookingDeadlines.comfortableClause: Event tickets can wait a little longer at this range.
bookingDeadlines.source: berlin-booking-deadline-planner: 'concerts, sports, festivals and special exhibitions are the easiest things to miss by waiting'

bookingDeadlines.label: A specific restaurant
bookingDeadlines.urgentNote: If there is one dinner you would be disappointed to lose, especially a weekend table, reserve it now. Everything else is fine left open.
bookingDeadlines.comfortableClause: Restaurant tables can still wait at this range.
bookingDeadlines.source: berlin-booking-deadline-planner: 'reserve only the meal you would be disappointed to lose, especially weekend dinner, casual food is usually better left open'

bookingDeadlineExcludedIds.tour: Handled live by the tour-day block instead of a generic deadline, since the real answer (which exact day, how many spots) is already computed from the live booking calendar. A generic reservation reminder here would either repeat or risk contradicting that live answer.
bookingDeadlineExcludedIds.transport: berlin-booking-deadline-planner treats this as never urgent ('do not over-plan this, buy the right ticket when you know the route'); no numeric threshold applies.

impactBoardNote: Additive dataset for the This Week Impact Board layer on the results surface. Kept separate from bigDates (a narrower precedent of the same shape, left untouched for backward compatibility) because impactBoard rows carry a fuller contract: impactType, severity, who/what/move breakdown and an area scope. Every row below was checked against an official source on the checkedAt date; a row is only ever shown while today's date is on or before its validThrough.

impactBoard.title: Berlin Marathon road closures
impactBoard.whatChanges: The marathon route and associated event areas bring major road closures across Berlin over race weekend. The organiser's interactive closure map is the authoritative street-by-street view.
impactBoard.whoItAffects: Anyone walking, cycling, using surface transport or driving near the race route on Saturday or Sunday.
impactBoard.timeNote: Race weekend is 26–27 September 2026. Exact closure and reopening times vary by street and must be checked on the organiser's current map.
impactBoard.visitorMove: Open the official interactive closure map for the exact street, then check BVG or VBB for the live public-transport route. Avoid planning repeated crossings of the course.

impactBoard.title: Festival of Lights
impactBoard.whatChanges: Landmarks across the centre are lit after dark for ten evenings under this year's programme.
impactBoard.whoItAffects: Evening sightseers heading to the usual illuminated landmarks such as the Brandenburg Gate, Museum Island and Berlin Cathedral.
impactBoard.timeNote: Ten evenings, 9–18 October 2026. Use the official programme for exact sites and illumination times.
impactBoard.visitorMove: Choose one or two confirmed programme sites in the same area instead of assuming every landmark is illuminated every evening.

impactBoard.title: German Unity Day
impactBoard.whatChanges: National public holiday. Most shops must close even though it falls on a Saturday. Narrow legal exceptions include some station and airport shops, pharmacies, petrol stations and certain tourist or special-range outlets.
impactBoard.whoItAffects: Visitors planning supermarket or other non-exempt shopping, or relying on an office or public service that day.
impactBoard.visitorMove: Do supermarket and other non-exempt shopping by Friday 2 October. Check museums, restaurants and any specific service individually instead of assuming normal Saturday hours.

impactBoard.title: Kastanienallee tram track renewal
impactBoard.whatChanges: BVG is renewing about 1.4km of tram track and two switches along Kastanienallee, Zionskirchstraße and Veteranenstraße, interrupting the M1 tram on this stretch.
impactBoard.whoItAffects: Anyone staying in Prenzlauer Berg and relying on the M1 tram through this stretch.
impactBoard.visitorMove: Check BVG or VBB for the replacement service on your travel day, or walk the affected stretch if that is practical.

impactBoard.title: Rosenthaler Straße tram works near Hackescher Markt
impactBoard.whatChanges: BVG is renewing the tram tracks in Rosenthaler Straße between Hackescher Markt and Weinmeisterstraße/Gipsstraße in two construction phases.
impactBoard.whoItAffects: Anyone staying in Mitte or relying on tram service around Hackescher Markt and Rosenthaler Straße.
impactBoard.visitorMove: Check BVG or VBB for the current replacement service and platform before travelling; the work changes phase on 22 October.

impactBoard.title: Pergamonmuseum main building closed
impactBoard.whatChanges: The Pergamonmuseum's main building is completely closed to the public for renovation. The North Wing and central building are not scheduled to reopen until 4 June 2027, and the South Wing stays closed until 2037.
impactBoard.whoItAffects: Anyone planning to see the Pergamon Altar or the Museum of Islamic Art inside the main building.
impactBoard.timeNote: Closed since 23 October 2023; North Wing and central building reopen 4 June 2027.
impactBoard.visitorMove: Consider Pergamonmuseum. Das Panorama nearby, or choose another Museum Island museum and check that museum's own opening and booking information for your date.

impactBoard.title: Reichstag dome closed for maintenance
impactBoard.whatChanges: The Reichstag dome is closed to visitors for cleaning and maintenance. The roof terrace can still be visited, but the dome audioguide is unavailable while the dome is closed.
impactBoard.whoItAffects: Anyone whose Berlin plan includes walking up inside the Reichstag dome during these dates.
impactBoard.timeNote: Dome closed all day from 14 through 18 September 2026.
impactBoard.visitorMove: Move the dome visit outside these dates. If your trip cannot move, register for the roof terrace and treat it as a different visit rather than expecting dome access.

impactBoard.title: Reichstag dome needs advance registration
impactBoard.whatChanges: Free dome visits require advance registration. The online request needs every participant's surname, first name and date of birth.
impactBoard.whoItAffects: Anyone planning to go up into the Reichstag dome, especially when the visit needs to fit a fixed part of the day.
impactBoard.timeNote: Admission slots run every 15 minutes; last admission is 21:45, except during announced closure periods.
impactBoard.visitorMove: Submit the online request once your dates are fixed. Without an advance booking, the Service Centre on Platz der Republik may issue a slot if places remain; confirmation must be issued at least 2 hours before the visit and visitors aged 16 or over need photo ID there.
